hypotheses.reasoning: session-cache was replaced at 02:28:13 and came back with 0 keys because no RDB snapshot was found (#115). Thirty seconds later account-svc reported a 95% cache miss ratio against a 2% baseline and began loading every lookup from accounts-db (#123). That stampede drove accounts-db to 484-493 of 500 connections at 95-98% CPU (#124, #133). Simple primary-key SELECTs then took 2.7-8.8s (#139, #161, #180), account-svc queries hit their 5s timeout (#138, #181), and edge-proxy returned /login 504s at 13-26s (#142 onward). Logins were healthy right before the cache restart (#110-#121). No deploy appears in the logs. The audit-consumer GC pause at 02:15 is a red herring because it came well before the onset.
Seen from account-svc, this looks like accounts-db queries timing out. But the database is slow because it is overloaded by the flood of cache misses, not because it hung on its own.
The accounts-db connection limit is nearly used up. This is a result of the stampede rather than the pool being too small for normal load.

verdict.recommendedAction: Warm session-cache again in a controlled way, by preloading hot accounts or rate-limiting cache fills with request coalescing, so many requests for the same key trigger only one database lookup. Shed or throttle login traffic to accounts-db until its CPU and connection count recover. Turn on RDB/AOF persistence or replicas for session-cache so a node replacement doesn't start it empty. Add stampede protection such as single-flight loading or jittered TTLs.
